_doc: One file per place; see places_build.py. Amounts in South Korean won. The debt component, history and facts are refreshed by pipeline/fetch_korea.py from the Ministry's Monthly Fiscal Trends PDF (needs pypdf); edit wording here, not numbers.
name: South Korea
publisher: Ministry of Planning and Budget (기획예산처), Republic of Korea
title: South Korea Debt Clock: Live Central Government Debt, Official Data
headline: central government debt
subject: The central government of South Korea
sum_note: South Korea's central government debt (중앙정부 채무), month-end, from the Ministry of Planning and Budget's Monthly Fiscal Trends. Cash basis, gross: government bonds, borrowings and Treasury obligations. Central government only.
scope_note: This is the central government debt (중앙정부 채무) in the Ministry's Monthly Fiscal Trends report: government bonds (Treasury bonds, national housing bonds and foreign exchange stabilisation bonds), borrowings and Treasury obligations, on a cash basis, at face value, in Korean won and before subtracting any assets. It is the series from which the Ministry builds the national debt (국가채무, D1) figure, which adds local government debt and is published for year-ends; that annual figure is shown as a fact. Debt of public corporations and unfunded pension liabilities are not included. Year-end figures and the current year's month-end figures are published in the same table.
trend_why: The Monthly Fiscal Trends table carries year-end rows and the current year's month-end rows only, so the trend is the official change from the closest earlier year-end or month-end in the table, and the page says which dates it compares. As the history builds, it moves to a twelve-month window.
legend: South Korea's central government debt is reported monthly, at month-end. Issuance happens in lumps at auctions and maturities, so the live number is a straight-line projection between official figures, shown here next to them.
cadence: Monthly. The Ministry publishes the Monthly Fiscal Trends about six weeks after the month ends.
after_text: , about six weeks after each month-end
next_update: The September 2026 month-end figure is expected in the Ministry's Monthly Fiscal Trends about six weeks after the month ends; this page re-bases to it automatically on the next daily build after it appears.

notes: Why this table: it is the Ministry's own monthly statement, the one the national press quotes, and the fetcher checks that bonds, borrowings and Treasury obligations add up to the debt in every row it reads.

Central versus national debt: the headline is central government debt. The Ministry's national debt (D1), which adds local governments, is larger and is published annually; the IMF's general government gross debt is wider again (it includes social security funds and non-financial public bodies). They are shown or described as different measures, not mixed.
Currency: Korean won. The World Debt Clock converts it to US dollars at the ECB's daily reference rate for KRW.
Language: the report is published in Korean; the page translates its labels and keeps the Korean terms next to them.
